A flag is carried at a public celebration.
Pexels · 38010823
Sharing a public celebration
There is more than one way to join a public celebration. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to
others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that checking arrangements makes a crowded event easier to navigate. For instance, we agree on a
meeting place before the parade begins. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also
leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that public enjoyment depends on consideration for others. For example, we keep walkways clear
and follow the event’s safety instructions. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one
person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail.
We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Explain the meaning before looking at the model answer. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example.
(Model: The two reasons are that checking arrangements makes a crowded event easier to navigate and that public
enjoyment depends on consideration for others. One example is that we agree on a meeting place before the parade begins.)
